title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-07-11
lineage: AUD > MC > Cass > Cass > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Fair audience recording of the July 11 1970 Fillmore East show, highlighted by a stellar acoustic set and high‑energy electric numbers.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – an intimate acoustic segment featuring “So Sad” and the first live Rosa Lee, followed by a thunderous electric set with Jerry’s pedal‑steel work and a soaring Morning Dew. The audience tape suffers from channel loss on the early songs, tape hiss and a “multi‑generation cassette” feel, but most listeners find it listenable given its historical rarity.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show highly (4–5 stars) for performance, while recording quality is described as fair to good; weighted average yields ~4.1.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Left channel only on first nine songs, noticeable tape hiss, multi‑generation cassette character, overall crude but listenable for a 1970 audience recording.

standout_songs: So Sad (to Watch Good Love Go Bad)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set opens with Easy Wind and three gospel numbers, includes a rare Everly Brothers cover; electric set kicks in with high energy, featuring Jerry’s pedal‑steel/possible wah‑wah and a powerful Morning Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar/pedal‑steel work is highlighted, with speculation about an early wah‑wah use.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir takes lead vocals on “Good Lovin’”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen (organ) plays a solo set despite having laryngitis; his keyboard contributions are noted.
